 Main Case No.: Writ Petition No.3270 of 2026
 Proceeding Sheet

entities.text: High Court Of Andhra Pradesh : At Amaravati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Sl. Date Order Office

No. Note
1. 04.02.2026 Srk, J
 Notice before admission.
Learned Government Pleader for Home  takes notice for respondent Nos.1 to 4 and seeks time for getting instructions.
Learned Standing Counsel for Union of India takes notice for respondent No.5 and seeks time for getting instructions.

Learned counsel for petitioner is permitted to take out personal notice to respondent Nos.6 and 7 through Registered Post with Acknowledgment Due and file proof of service in the Registry within a period of four (04) weeks.
Heard.
Perused the record.
The present Writ Petition is filed challenging the Look Out Circular issued against the petitioner in connection with Crime No.60 of 2024 of Mahila UPS, Visakhapatnam.

A perusal of the material on record goes to show that petitioner is a Non-Resident Indian, SL. DATE ORDER OFFICE NO. NOTE employed in USA; he married 7th respondent and they both resided in USA for some period.

A perusal of the material on record further goes to show that Look Out Circular (LOC) was issued pursuant to registration of a case in Crime No.60 of 2025 of Mahila UPS, Visakhapatnam for the offences punishable under Sections 498A of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961 basing on the report lodged by 7th respondent.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioner that a decree of divorce was passed on 07.11.2019 by the Superior Court of California, USA, dissolving the marriage held between petitioner and 7th respondent vide Case No.18FL002092, and the same was confirmed by the Additional Family Court,
Visakhapatnam on 24.03.2020 vide O.P.No.413 of 2019.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would further contend that pursuant to Look Out Circular, there is a threat of arrest to the petitioner and it SL.
DATE ORDER OFFICE NO.

NOTE would be a hurdle for the petitioner to travel and in each and every Airport he would be stopped and his credentials would be questioned by the Immigration and he would be restrained in the Airport without issuing Unknown vs 4.02.2026 Srk on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112036335/
1 boarding pass.

A perusal of the material on record goes to show that this Court vide Order, dated 15.12.2025 in Criminal Petition No.12898 of 2025, stayed the proceedings in FIR vide Crime No.60 of 2025 of Mahila UPS, Visakhapatnam.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, marriage between petitioner and 7th respondent was dissolved by a competent Court in USA, on contest, and the same was affirmed by the learned Additional Family Court, Visakhapatnam in OP No.413 of 2019.
By virtue of opening of the Look Out Circular, personal liberty of the person is curtailed.
The LOCs are only the circular instructions that have been issued by the police only with a view to detain a person or to see that he will cooperate SL.
DATE ORDER OFFICE NO.
NOTE with the trial in a criminal case.

Of late, in each and every case that has been registered under Sections 498A IPC, it has become common for the respondent/police, without looking into the aspects whether the petitioner is cooperating with the trial or evading arrest, to open the LOCs in mechanical manner.

It is essential that the police have to open LOCs against the persons who are the accused for grave offences or the persons who are involved in financial irregularities or the offences which are against the Society.
In such cases, the respondent/police can resort in opening the LOCs against the accused, not permitting them to leave the country.

The offences alleged against the petitioner in Crime No.60 of 2025 of Women UPS, Visakhapatnam are under Sections 498A IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the DP Act and, if the petitioner is not permitted to travel abroad as a part of his employment, by virtue of opening LOC against him,
petitioner would suffer irreparable SL.
DATE ORDER
OFFICE NO. NOTE loss.
These aspects have to be seen on the touchstone of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

By virtue of opening LOC,
personal liberty of the person would be affected.
On mere registration of a case for a matrimonial office, opening of the LOC will affect the career of a person.
The matter requires examination.

In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, there shall be interim suspension of operation of Look Out Circular issued by the respondents against the petitioner in Crime No.60 of 2024 of Mahila UPS, Visakhapatnam.
List the matter after four (04) weeks.

SRK, J Note:
Issue CC today.

B/o.
